original.target_description: Nguyen et al., Experiment 2; American and Japanese final sample, independent and interdependent contexts; Experiment 2: perceived usefulness of promotion-focus recall for eager versus vigilant tasks; simple effect of task in the promotion-recall condition. Bayesian mixed-effects model of within-culture standardized usefulness ratings.

n.sample_role: Participants in the analytic mixed-effects model (United States and Japan; both contexts)
n.exclusions: 32 American and 10 Japanese participants excluded. General exclusion criteria include distraction, low seriousness, language fluency, and MTurk location/repeated-location restrictions.

es.metric: βest (Bayesian coefficient; outcome standardized within culture)

p.location: p. 813 (PDF p. 7), Task-motivation fit, promotion recall simple effect

replication.target_description: Vaughn et al., replication of American-independent conditions of Experiment 2; Experiment 2: perceived usefulness of promotion-focus recall for eager versus vigilant tasks; simple effect of task in the promotion-recall condition. Paired-samples t-test.

n.sample_role: American participants in the final analytic repeated-measures sample
n.exclusions: Two other participants excluded for not answering five or more of 24 stimulus-material questions.
n.location: Study 2, Method—Participants; Table 1; Table 3 degrees of freedom
n.quote: Table 1 shows characteristics of the final sample (N = 100) for our replication of Nguyen et al.’s (2021) Study 2.

es.location: Replication of the American-Independent Conditions of Study 2, Conducted March 2022; follow-up paired-samples t-tests

p.location: Replication of the American-Independent Conditions of Study 2, Conducted March 2022; follow-up paired-samples t-tests

reported_success.quote: We replicated findings from the American-independent conditions of Nguyen et al.’s (2021) Experiment 2.

notes: Original results are the full cross-cultural model, not the American-independent reanalysis quoted secondarily in the replication. Original main-paper analyses are Bayesian and print HDIs rather than p values; no frequentist p has been attached to a Bayesian coefficient. Retrieved published pagination differs from the supplied locator. Replication d is explicitly printed by the authors (omnibus effects described as equivalent d); no conversion performed here. Reported success uses authors’ explicit study-level narrative replication verdict, not an inference from significance.
